ad_clicks.description: Track the number of times users clicked on ads in your app. Clicks indicate user engagement with ads and can help you understand which ad placements and formats are most effective.

measures.description: The total number of times users clicked on ads. Each click represents a user interaction with an advertisement.

ad_monetized_customers.description: Track the number of unique customers with at least one recorded ad impression. This helps you understand the size of your ad-monetized user base and identify trends in ad engagement.

measures.description: The count of unique customers with at least one recorded ad impression. Each customer is counted once per period, regardless of how many ads they viewed or how much revenue they generated.

paywall_abandonment.description:
Paywall Abandonment measures the proportion of customer-paywall pairs that did not result in an initial conversion on calendar days 0 through 3. It breaks abandonment into purchase cancellations and bounces.

This chart is cohorted by the first paywall impression date for each customer-paywall pair. A pair is abandoned if no initial conversion occurs on calendar days 0 through 3. Total abandonment combines bounced and cancelled pairs.

This chart only tracks impressions and conversions from RevenueCat Paywalls. Paywalls implemented with custom code are not tracked.

Tracking paywall abandonment helps identify friction points in your monetization flow. High bounce rates may indicate pricing or value proposition issues, while high cancellation rates might suggest payment flow problems or buyer's remorse at the final step.

measures.description: The number of unique customer-paywall pairs first seen during the cohort period.
The total number of customer-paywall pairs that bounced or cancelled.
The percentage of customer-paywall pairs that bounced or cancelled.

app_store_save_outcomes.description: App Store Save Outcomes is used with Apple's Retention Message API feature. This chart measures the total number of saved retention messages in each period, broken down by outcome: redeemed promotional offer, redeemed alternate plan, or no purchase.

measures.description: The number of saved retention messages in the period.

actives.description:
Active Subscriptions shows the number of paid subscriptions granting access at the end of each period charted. Billing-retry periods remain active while access continues.

Subscriptions that have auto-renew disabled are still counted in Active Subscriptions. Refunded subscriptions are counted as active between their start date and their refund date.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, Active Subscriptions uses the cycle each subscription was in on that date. For example, when a subscription renews from Cycle 1 into Cycle 2, it moves to Cycle 2 on the renewal date; before that it counts in Cycle 1.

Active subscriptions is important as a measure of the number of individual, recurring relationships you are currently serving and is a proxy for the size of the business.

measures.description: The number of paid subscriptions granting access at the end of the period.

actives_movement.description:
Active Subscriptions Movement measures the change in Active Subscriptions caused by new subscriptions, resubscriptions, and net paid-access losses.

New Actives are first paid subscriptions started in the period. Resubscription Actives are subscriptions restarted after previously churning. Churned Actives is the net decrease from subscriptions losing paid access; billing recoveries, access restorations, and resumed pauses reduce it and can make it negative. Product changes net to zero in the total Movement, but their two sides can surface through Churned Actives when filters are applied. Movement is New Actives + Resubscription Actives - Churned Actives.

Dissecting the movement of your Active Subscriptions is a good way to understand what is causing your subscription base to grow or shrink.

measures.description: New Actives is the number of first paid subscriptions started in the period, including trial conversions, paid introductory offers, and direct subscriptions.
Resubscription Actives is the number of subscriptions that were previously churned and re-subscribed in the period.
The net number of subscriptions that lost paid access in the period, after subtracting billing recoveries, access restorations, and resumed pauses.
New Actives + Resubscription Actives - Churned Actives, the net change in Active Subscriptions during the period.

actives_new.description:
Paid Subscriptions measures paid subscription starts and paid-to-paid product changes in a given period.

The chart splits that count by Trial Conversions, Intro Offers, Direct Subscriptions, Product Changes, and Resubscriptions. It can be segmented by the available dimensions to understand what's driving your paid subscription performance.

measures.description: New paid subscriptions from trials that converted to paid in the period. If a customer's trial expired without conversion, and the customer resubscribes to the same product at a later point, it is counted as a resubscription, not a trial conversion.
New paid subscriptions with paid introductory offers started in the period.
New paid subscriptions without a trial or introductory offer that started in the period.
Paid subscriptions that started due to a product change during the period.
Paid subscriptions from customers who resubscribed after previously churning during the period.
Total paid subscription starts and paid-to-paid product changes in the period.

arr.description:
Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, is an annualized estimation of your recurring revenue. It is computed by multiplying MRR by 12. Non-recurring subscriptions, consumable, or one-time purchases are not computed in ARR. Also, a subscription contributes to ARR until it expires, the auto-renew status has no effect.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, ARR uses the cycle each subscription was in on that date. For example, when a subscription renews from Cycle 1 into Cycle 2, its ARR moves to Cycle 2 on the renewal date; its earlier ARR remains in Cycle 1.

ARR is an important metric to track as it is a common benchmark for subscription companies and is a good way to assess scale of your existing business.

measures.description: Annual Recurring Revenue at the end of the period.

churn.description:
Churn is the percentage of paid subscriptions that were lost during a given period.

Actives measures paid subscriptions granting access at the beginning of a given period. Churned Actives measures net paid-access losses during the period; billing recoveries, other access restorations, and subscriptions resuming after a pause reduce this count and can make it negative. Unlike Active Subscriptions Movement, this measure includes subscriptions replaced during product changes.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, each subscription counts in the cycle it was in on that date. A renewal moves it into the next cycle and is not churn. A subscription that loses access and recovers into the next cycle counts as churned in its old cycle, and its recovery reduces Churned Actives in the new one. Each cycle's losses are compared with its subscriptions at the start of the period, so products shorter than the chart's resolution can show rates above 100%.

A stable or declining churn rate indicates a healthy, growing business. However, keep in mind that churn can be relatively high for mobile apps when compared to web SaaS products.

measures.description: The number of paid subscriptions granting access at the beginning of the period.

The net number of paid subscriptions that stopped granting access during the period, after subtracting billing recoveries, other access restorations, and subscriptions resuming after a pause. This includes subscriptions replaced during product changes.
Net paid-access losses during the period as a percentage of paid subscriptions granting access at the beginning of the period.

cohort_explorer.description:
The Cohort Explorer allows you to measure the performance of various cohort definitions over time and across multiple performance measurements.

Cohorts can be defined as New Customers grouped by customer cohort date (the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase), Initial Conversions, or New Paying Customers from a given period. Their performance can then be measured by Revenue, Gross revenue before refunds or Ad revenue generated in each period, Realized LTV as of a given period, or the count of paid subscriptions that remain active at each period boundary.

Revenue measures include ad revenue. In Initial Conversions and New Paying Customers, ad revenue counts from the customer's first purchase day. Filters on customer attributes, such as country or attribution, leave ad revenue out.

The final, incomplete period is indicated with a hashed background to illustrate that this period's performance may change over time.
Keep in mind that each cohort definition creates unique groups of customers, and therefore they should not be directly compared with each other.

conversion_to_paying.description:
Conversion to Paying measures what proportion of new customers make any payment.

Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. Each period measures the number of New Customers whose cohort date falls in that period, and the number of those customers that are now Paying Customers.

The conversion timeframe selector sets the maximum amount of time each period's cohort has to convert within for accurate historical comparisons.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.
Customers whose first paid purchase occurred on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, minus customers whose first paid purchase was refunded during the same window.
The percentage of customers whose first paid purchase occurred on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, net of first-purchase refunds during the same window.

customers_new.description: New Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. In RevenueCat, the term "customer" refers to the person using an app, regardless of whether they have yet made a purchase. You can use our conversion charts to measure the portion of these customers that then start trials, convert to paid, etc. Any customers who are aliased to another customer will be excluded from this chart.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.

initial_conversion.description:
Initial conversion measures what proportion of new customers start any subscription (including trial) or make any purchase.

Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. Each period measures the number of New Customers whose cohort date falls in that period, and the number of those customers that have converted on any product (Initial Conversions). For apps that exclusively rely on products with trials, the initial conversion rate is equal to the trial start rate. As in Conversion to Paying, an Initial Conversion whose purchase is refunded is removed from the conversion timeframes that include the refund. A trial start is never removed, even if the payment it later converted into is refunded.

The conversion timeframe selector sets the maximum amount of time each period's cohort has to convert within for accurate historical comparisons.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.

The number of customers that converted to any product, including a trial, paid subscription, or one-time purchase, on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, minus customers whose initial conversion purchase was refunded during the same window.
The percentage of customers that converted to any product on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, net of refunded initial conversion purchases during the same window.

ltv_per_customer.description:
Realized LTV (Lifetime Value) per Customer (also known as Average Revenue per User, ARPU) measures the actual gross revenue generated by a customer cohort, minus refunds processed within the selected Customer Lifetime, divided by the number of customers in that cohort. Purchase revenue and ad revenue are included.
Customers are cohorted by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. The “Customer Lifetime” selector defines the final calendar day included in the LTV calculation. For example, 30 days includes revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after each customer's cohort date.

Realized LTV per Customer can be used as a tool to understand the profitability of (paid) acquisition, compare the impact of product price changes over time, and much more.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.
The total gross revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus refunds processed during the same window.
The total proceeds generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus refunds processed during the same window.
The average gross revenue per customer on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, after subtracting refunds processed during the same window.

ltv_per_paying_customer.description:
Realized LTV (Lifetime Value) per Paying Customer (also known as Average Revenue per Paying User, ARPPU) measures the actual gross revenue generated by a customer cohort, minus refunds processed within the selected Customer Lifetime, divided by the number of paying customers in that cohort. Purchase revenue and ad revenue from customers who become paying customers within that lifetime are included.
Customers are cohorted by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. The “Customer Lifetime” selector defines the final calendar day included in the LTV calculation. For example, 30 days includes revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after each customer's cohort date.
Customers whose first paid purchase is refunded within the selected Customer Lifetime are removed from the paying-customer count.
Realized LTV per Paying Customer can be used as a tool to understand the profitability of (paid) acquisition, compare the impact of product price changes over time, and much more.

measures.description: Customers whose first paid purchase occurred on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus customers whose first paid purchase was refunded during the same window.
The total gross revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus refunds processed during the same window.
The average gross revenue per paying customer on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, after subtracting refunds processed during the same window.

mrr.description:
Monthly Recurring Revenue, or MRR, is a way of normalizing the scale of your business to better understand your velocity or size. It doesn't map directly to revenue, but it is a useful standardization.

MRR is computed by "normalizing" subscriptions to a 1-month period. For example, a subscription that is $8 per month, will contribute $8 to MRR while it is active. An annual subscription that costs $120 per year will contribute $10 dollars per month to MRR for 12 months. This normalizing of all durations to a 1 month period makes it easier to compare different subscriptions of different durations together.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, MRR uses the cycle each subscription was in on that date. For example, when a subscription renews from Cycle 1 into Cycle 2, its MRR moves to Cycle 2 on the renewal date; its earlier MRR remains in Cycle 1.

MRR is an important measure because it not only captures the size of your subscriber base, but translates that into a real velocity metric for your business. MRR and ARR are considered the standard velocity metrics for subscription software companies.

measures.description: Monthly Recurring Revenue at the end of the period.

mrr_movement.description:
MRR Movement shows how new subscriptions, resubscriptions, expansion, churn, and contraction affect MRR.

Movement is New MRR + Resubscription MRR + Expansion MRR - Churned MRR - Contraction MRR.

Looking at MRR Movement is important to understand the factors that cause your MRR to increase or decrease over a period and give insight into what grows or contracts your business.

measures.description: MRR contributed by New Subscriptions.
MRR contributed by customers who resubscribed after lapsing.

MRR added when continuing subscriptions begin generating more MRR, such as after product changes, price changes, offer periods, higher-contribution renewals and recoveries, or an exchange rate change causes a subscription to generate more MRR.
MRR removed when paid access ends, a payment is refunded or adjusted downward, or a renewal or billing recovery brings in no revenue.

MRR removed when continuing subscriptions begin generating less MRR, such as after product changes, price changes, offer periods, lower-contribution renewals and recoveries, or an exchange rate change causes a subscription to generate less MRR.
New MRR + Resubscription MRR + Expansion MRR - Churned MRR - Contraction MRR, the net change in MRR during the period.

prediction_explorer.description:
The Prediction Explorer allows you to measure the gross predicted lifetime value (LTV) of various customer cohorts over time to estimate the long-term revenue that may be driven by those cohorts. We generate predicted revenue based on the prior retention rates of subscriptions on the same product, or of a mix of fallback dimensions when sufficient data for the purchased product is unavailable, and then tailoring that prediction based on the cancellation behavior of each individual subscription.

Cohorts can be defined as cohorts of New Customers, Initial Conversions, or New Paying Customers from a given period. Predictions are provided with either a yellow cell shading, indicating a low-volume cohort size where therefore the prediction is low confidence, or a light green cell shading which represent our predictions for cohorts with a sufficient sample size.

Please use caution when making decisions based on predicted future performance, and review the linked documentation below to understand the current limitations of the prediction model.

refund_rate.description:
The Refund Rate chart shows the number of paid subscription transactions and one-time purchases in each time period and what proportion of these transactions was refunded. This includes new subscriptions, renewals, resubscriptions, and paid product changes. Trial starts are excluded because they have no revenue and cannot be refunded.

Refunds are counted in the period of the original paid transaction, not the period when the refund was processed. This means the Refund Rate for a prior period can change when a new refund is recorded. When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, the chart uses the cycle at the time of the original transaction.

The Refund Rate is an important indicator whether your customers are getting the value they expected when they started their subscription.

measures.description: The total number of paid, non-trial subscription transactions and one-time purchases during the period.
The number of transactions that were refunded grouped by the purchase date.
The percentage of transactions from the period that have been refunded. The rate can change later when new refunds are recorded.

refund_request.description:
This chart tracks App Store and Google Play refund and chargeback events. It breaks events down by resolution status—whether the refund was granted, declined, reversed, or is still awaiting the store's decision. Each request is counted in the period RevenueCat received it, and its outcome updates as store notifications arrive.
To receive these events in RevenueCat, configure App Store Server Notifications and Google Play notifications. For the most accurate and timely App Store data, we recommend using Apple's V2 notifications.

measures.description: The number of refund requests granted in the period.

The number of refund requests classified as declined, including store-declined requests and unresolved requests without an observed grant after 2 days for App Store or 7 days for Google Play. Google Play declines are inferred because Google does not send decline events.
The number of refunds reversed in the period.
The number of refund requests without a final outcome that remain within the store's fallback window: 2 days for App Store or 7 days for Google Play.
Total refund requests in the period.

refunds.description: The Refunds chart shows refunds processed during a period, plus downward subscription payment adjustments recorded during that period. Refunded Transactions counts store refund events only. You can select between Refunded Revenue, Refunded Revenue (net of taxes), or Refunded Proceeds as the definition to visualize in the chart.

measures.description: Gross revenue from refunds processed and downward subscription payment adjustments recorded in the period, rounded to the nearest whole number.
The number of store refund events grouped by the date the refund was processed. Downward payment adjustments without a refund event do not increase this count.

revenue.description: Revenue displays the revenue generated during a period. This number will usually be a little higher than MRR as it is un-normalized and all the revenue from an annual subscription is charted the period it starts or is renewed. This chart also displays all revenue from non-consumable and consumable purchases, non-renewing subscriptions, and ads. You can select between Revenue, Revenue (net of taxes), Proceeds, or Gross revenue before refunds as the revenue definition to visualize in the chart. When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, each transaction uses the cycle that applied when it occurred, so later renewals do not move earlier revenue to another cycle.

measures.description: The net revenue generated in a given period; which is total revenue after refunds and downward subscription payment adjustments, minus our estimate of revenue deducted from the stores for taxes and commission.
The count of revenue-generating purchase transactions in the period. Refunds do not reduce this count.
The total number of times ads were successfully displayed to users. Each impression represents one instance of an ad being shown.

subscription_retention.description:
Subscription Retention measures how paying subscriptions renew and retain over time by cohorts.

When segmenting by subscription start date, cohorts are segmented by the start of a paid subscription. Period 0 is the initial paid period; later completed periods show how many subscriptions reached that paid renewal period, whether or not auto-renew is still enabled. When segmenting by other fields, cohorts include all paid subscriptions started within the specified date range and show the portion that reached each paid period out of those with an opportunity to do so.

The final, incomplete period is indicated with a hashed background and shows how many subscriptions are set to renew by the end of the period, taking into account the auto-renewal preference of the subscriptions.

subscription_status.description:
The Subscription Status chart breaks down Active Subscriptions, Active Trials, MRR, ARR, or Subscription Revenue by the current status of the underlying subscription that currently grants access and contributes to that measure.

A subscription will have a status of Billing Issue if it's currently in a grace period or a billing retry where access remains active. Billing retries where access has ended are not included in the chart. Set to Cancel includes subscriptions that will not renew, will pause, or require price-increase consent. Set to Renew includes subscriptions that will renew, change products, or have already renewed. Other states are shown as Unknown.

Each measure can then be filtered or segmented by values like Product Duration, Expiration Month, and more to understand how the portion Set to Cancel or in a Billing Issue state is affected by these dimensions.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, the chart uses the cycle from each subscription's latest current event.

measures.description: The total number of currently active subscriptions.
The number of currently active subscriptions in the Set to Renew status, including subscriptions set to renew, change products, or already renewed.
The number of currently active subscriptions that are set to cancel at the end of their current period.

The number of currently active subscriptions that were set to renew at the end of their prior period, but failed to do so due to a billing issue, and whose access remains active during a grace period or billing retry.
The portion of currently active subscriptions in the Set to Renew status.
measures.display_name: Active Subscriptions Set to Renew Percentage

measures.description: The portion of currently active subscriptions that are set to cancel at the end of their current period.
measures.display_name: Active Subscriptions Set to Cancel Percentage

measures.description: The portion of currently active subscriptions that were set to renew at the end of their prior period, but failed to do so due to a billing issue, and whose access remains active during a grace period or billing retry.

trials.description:
Active Trials shows the number of active trials at the end of the period. This includes all trials, regardless of whether they are set to auto-convert on completion.

The volume of Active Trials is a good leading indicator to growth of Active Subscriptions and therefore MRR. If the volume of active trials is increasing or decreasing it indicates that your business may be accelerating or decelerating respectively. The Active Trials Movement chart can help you understand these movements.

measures.description: The number of free trials granting access at the end of the period.

trials_movement.description:
Active Trials Movement breaks down the inputs to the Active Trials chart and gives you a picture of how your active trial base is evolving.

New Trials includes trial starts and trial-to-trial product changes. Expired Trials includes trials that stopped granting access and product changes away from a trial, reduced by access restorations. Trial-to-trial product changes add one to each side and therefore net to zero in Movement.

Understanding the dynamics of your trial base is important for understanding leading indicators of the growth of your business.

measures.description: Trial starts and trial-to-trial product changes in the period.
Trials that stopped granting access and product changes away from a trial, reduced by access restorations.
New Trials - Expired Trials, the net change in Active Trials during the period.

trials_new.description:
New Trials counts the trials that started during the period. Changing product while staying in a trial is not a new trial and is not counted here; the Active Trials Movement chart includes those, because Active Trials has to move the trial between products.
Unlike the conversion charts, which group customers by the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase, this chart attributes each trial to the date that trial started. Each subscription trial is counted, so a customer who starts trials on two subscriptions contributes two New Trials but only one Trial Start in the Trial Conversion Funnel.
The New Trials chart can be used to track volume in this key top of funnel metric, and segment it by key dimensions for your business to understand what's driving your performance.

measures.description: The number of trials that started in the period.

customers_active.description: Active Customers counts the approximate number of unique customers for whom RevenueCat recorded SDK activity during the selected period. A customer with activity multiple times or on multiple days is counted once in that period. In RevenueCat, the term "customer" refers to the person using an app, regardless of whether they have yet made a purchase. You can use our conversion charts to measure the portion of these customers that then start trials, convert to paid, etc. Data is only accurate for the last 28 days. Data before that may be inaccurate or zero.

measures.description: The approximate number of unique customers for whom RevenueCat recorded SDK activity during the period. Each customer is counted once per period.

trial_conversion.description:
The Trial Conversion Funnel measures the conversion of customers starting free trials, through their conversion into paying subscriptions.

Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. Each period measures the number of New Customers whose cohort date falls in that period.

A customer enters the funnel when they start a free trial no later than their first conversion. For example, a trial started after the customer already bought a one-time product is excluded. Each qualifying customer contributes once to Started Trials. Their outcome can reflect a later trial. If they abandon the first trial but a later trial becomes their first paid purchase, they are counted as converted, not abandoned.

The Start Rate is a valuable way of measuring how compelling your value proposition is, but Conversion Rate is the real measure of how effectively that value proposition has been delivered through your product during the trial period.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.
The number of customers in the cohort who started at least one qualifying trial.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial converted into a paid subscription. Later refunds do not remove the conversion.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial is active and set to auto-convert on completion.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial is active and not set to auto-convert on completion.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial no longer grants access but is not yet terminal, such as during billing retry or a pause.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial expired without converting.
The percentage of New Customers who started at least one qualifying trial.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial converted into a paid subscription. Active trials are not yet conversions.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial is active and set to auto-convert.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial is active and not set to auto-convert.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial no longer grants access but is not yet terminal.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial expired without converting.

trial_conversion_rate.description:
The Trial Conversion Rate chart measures the number of trials that started in a given period, and the portion of them that converted to a paid subscription. Each trial is counted separately.

Trial Conversion Rate is important to track so that you can understand how likelihood to pay changes over time and by various dimensions.

Conversion Rate counts pending trials as not converted, so periods whose trials are still running read low until those trials end. Select Conversion Rate (Completed Trials) to leave pending trials out, which makes recent periods and newly launched stores comparable sooner.

Please note that the number of Trial Starts reported in each period in this chart will differ from the same period of the Trial Conversion Funnel, since the funnel is grouped by customer cohort date—the earliest date a customer was first seen or made their first purchase—not by trial start date.

measures.description: The number of trials that started in the period.
The number of those trials that converted to paid. Later refunds do not remove the conversion.
The number of those trials that expired without converting.
The number of those trials that have not yet converted or expired.
The number of those trials that have converted or expired.
The portion of trials that started in the period that converted to paid. Pending trials count as not converted.

trial_cancellation.description:
The Trial Cancellation chart measures the portion of trials that started in a given period and were canceled within a specified period of time since their start date. Each trial is counted separately.

A "canceled" trial is one that expired without converting to paid, where the customer turned off auto-renewal at some point during the trial (while it still granted access). Cancellations are timed by the customer's last in-trial opt-out, so a trial that is cancelled, re-enabled, and cancelled again is measured by that final cancellation. A trial whose customer opts out but which then converts is not counted as a cancellation.

Cancellation is one of the reasons a trial can expire without converting. The others are shown in the breakdown — billing failures (the payment was in a retry or grace period at expiry) and lapsed trials (expired with no opt-out and no billing signal).

The Cancellation Timeframe selector measures whether the last in-trial opt-out occurred within 1, 2, 5, or 7 days of each trial's start, with each day measured as 24 hours. Unbounded includes an opt-out at any point during the trial.

measures.description: The number of trials that started in the period.
The number of those trials that expired without converting and whose last in-trial opt-out happened within 168 hours of its start.
The number of those trials that expired without converting while payment was in a billing-retry or grace period.
The number of those trials that ended without converting and without an observed opt-out or billing-failure signal, including trials past their end date without a terminal expired event.
The percentage of trials that started in the period that expired without converting and whose last in-trial opt-out happened within 168 hours of its start.

non-subscription_purchases.description: Non-subscription purchases include consumable, non-consumable, lifetime, and non-renewing subscription purchases; none renew automatically.

measures.description: The number of non-subscription purchases that occurred in a period.

ad_revenue.description: Track the total revenue generated from ads in your app. This is your primary monetization metric, showing how much income your ad placements are generating.

measures.description: The total number of times users clicked on ads.
The total number of times ads were displayed to users.
The total amount earned from ads during the period.

ad_impressions.description: Track the total number of times ads were displayed to users in your app. Impressions represent your ad exposure and are the foundation for calculating other key metrics like CTR and eCPM.

measures.description: The total number of times ads were successfully displayed to users. Each impression represents one instance of an ad being shown.

measures.description: The total number of times users clicked on ads. Each click represents a user interaction with an advertisement.

measures.description: The count of unique customers with at least one recorded ad impression. Each customer is counted once per period, regardless of how many ads they viewed or how much revenue they generated.

measures.description: The number of paid subscriptions granting access at the end of the period.

actives_movement.description:
Active Subscriptions Movement measures the change in Active Subscriptions caused by new subscriptions, resubscriptions, and net paid-access losses.

New Actives are first paid subscriptions started in the period. Resubscription Actives are subscriptions restarted after previously churning. Churned Actives is the net decrease from subscriptions losing paid access; billing recoveries, access restorations, and resumed pauses reduce it and can make it negative. Product changes net to zero in the total Movement, but their two sides can surface through Churned Actives when filters are applied. Movement is New Actives + Resubscription Actives - Churned Actives.

Dissecting the movement of your Active Subscriptions is a good way to understand what is causing your subscription base to grow or shrink.

measures.description: New Actives is the number of first paid subscriptions started in the period, including trial conversions, paid introductory offers, and direct subscriptions.
Resubscription Actives is the number of subscriptions that were previously churned and re-subscribed in the period.
The net number of subscriptions that lost paid access in the period, after subtracting billing recoveries, access restorations, and resumed pauses.
New Actives + Resubscription Actives - Churned Actives, the net change in Active Subscriptions during the period.

actives_new.description:
Paid Subscriptions measures paid subscription starts and paid-to-paid product changes in a given period.

The chart splits that count by Trial Conversions, Intro Offers, Direct Subscriptions, Product Changes, and Resubscriptions. It can be segmented by the available dimensions to understand what's driving your paid subscription performance.

measures.description: New paid subscriptions from trials that converted to paid in the period. If a customer's trial expired without conversion, and the customer resubscribes to the same product at a later point, it is counted as a resubscription, not a trial conversion.
New paid subscriptions with paid introductory offers started in the period.
New paid subscriptions without a trial or introductory offer that started in the period.
Paid subscriptions that started due to a product change during the period.
Paid subscriptions from customers who resubscribed after previously churning during the period.
Total paid subscription starts and paid-to-paid product changes in the period.

arr.description:
Annual Recurring Revenue, or ARR, is an annualized estimation of your recurring revenue. It is computed by multiplying MRR by 12. Non-recurring subscriptions, consumable, or one-time purchases are not computed in ARR. Also, a subscription contributes to ARR until it expires, the auto-renew status has no effect.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, ARR uses the cycle each subscription was in on that date. For example, when a subscription renews from Cycle 1 into Cycle 2, its ARR moves to Cycle 2 on the renewal date; its earlier ARR remains in Cycle 1.

ARR is an important metric to track as it is a common benchmark for subscription companies and is a good way to assess scale of your existing business.

measures.description: Annual Recurring Revenue at the end of the period.

churn.description:
Churn is the percentage of paid subscriptions that were lost during a given period.

Actives measures paid subscriptions granting access at the beginning of a given period. Churned Actives measures net paid-access losses during the period; billing recoveries, other access restorations, and subscriptions resuming after a pause reduce this count and can make it negative. Unlike Active Subscriptions Movement, this measure includes subscriptions replaced during product changes.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, each subscription counts in the cycle it was in on that date. A renewal moves it into the next cycle and is not churn. A subscription that loses access and recovers into the next cycle counts as churned in its old cycle, and its recovery reduces Churned Actives in the new one. Each cycle's losses are compared with its subscriptions at the start of the period, so products shorter than the chart's resolution can show rates above 100%.

A stable or declining churn rate indicates a healthy, growing business. However, keep in mind that churn can be relatively high for mobile apps when compared to web SaaS products.

measures.description: The number of paid subscriptions granting access at the beginning of the period.

The net number of paid subscriptions that stopped granting access during the period, after subtracting billing recoveries, other access restorations, and subscriptions resuming after a pause. This includes subscriptions replaced during product changes.
Net paid-access losses during the period as a percentage of paid subscriptions granting access at the beginning of the period.

cohort_explorer.description:
The Cohort Explorer allows you to measure the performance of various cohort definitions over time and across multiple performance measurements.

Cohorts can be defined as New Customers grouped by customer cohort date (the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase), Initial Conversions, or New Paying Customers from a given period. Their performance can then be measured by Revenue, Gross revenue before refunds or Ad revenue generated in each period, Realized LTV as of a given period, or the count of paid subscriptions that remain active at each period boundary.

Revenue measures include ad revenue. In Initial Conversions and New Paying Customers, ad revenue counts from the customer's first purchase day. Filters on customer attributes, such as country or attribution, leave ad revenue out.

The final, incomplete period is indicated with a hashed background to illustrate that this period's performance may change over time.
Keep in mind that each cohort definition creates unique groups of customers, and therefore they should not be directly compared with each other.

conversion_to_paying.description:
Conversion to Paying measures what proportion of new customers make any payment.

Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. Each period measures the number of New Customers whose cohort date falls in that period, and the number of those customers that are now Paying Customers.

The conversion timeframe selector sets the maximum amount of time each period's cohort has to convert within for accurate historical comparisons.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.
Customers whose first paid purchase occurred on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, minus customers whose first paid purchase was refunded during the same window.
The percentage of customers whose first paid purchase occurred on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, net of first-purchase refunds during the same window.

customers_new.description: New Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. In RevenueCat, the term "customer" refers to the person using an app, regardless of whether they have yet made a purchase. You can use our conversion charts to measure the portion of these customers that then start trials, convert to paid, etc. Any customers who are aliased to another customer will be excluded from this chart.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.

initial_conversion.description:
Initial conversion measures what proportion of new customers start any subscription (including trial) or make any purchase.

Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. Each period measures the number of New Customers whose cohort date falls in that period, and the number of those customers that have converted on any product (Initial Conversions). For apps that exclusively rely on products with trials, the initial conversion rate is equal to the trial start rate. As in Conversion to Paying, an Initial Conversion whose purchase is refunded is removed from the conversion timeframes that include the refund. A trial start is never removed, even if the payment it later converted into is refunded.

The conversion timeframe selector sets the maximum amount of time each period's cohort has to convert within for accurate historical comparisons.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.

The number of customers that converted to any product, including a trial, paid subscription, or one-time purchase, on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, minus customers whose initial conversion purchase was refunded during the same window.
The percentage of customers that converted to any product on calendar days 0 through 7 after they were first seen, net of refunded initial conversion purchases during the same window.

ltv_per_customer.description:
Realized LTV (Lifetime Value) per Customer (also known as Average Revenue per User, ARPU) measures the actual gross revenue generated by a customer cohort, minus refunds processed within the selected Customer Lifetime, divided by the number of customers in that cohort. Purchase revenue and ad revenue are included.
Customers are cohorted by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. The “Customer Lifetime” selector defines the final calendar day included in the LTV calculation. For example, 30 days includes revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after each customer's cohort date.

Realized LTV per Customer can be used as a tool to understand the profitability of (paid) acquisition, compare the impact of product price changes over time, and much more.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.
The total gross revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus refunds processed during the same window.
The total proceeds generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus refunds processed during the same window.
The average gross revenue per customer on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, after subtracting refunds processed during the same window.

ltv_per_paying_customer.description:
Realized LTV (Lifetime Value) per Paying Customer (also known as Average Revenue per Paying User, ARPPU) measures the actual gross revenue generated by a customer cohort, minus refunds processed within the selected Customer Lifetime, divided by the number of paying customers in that cohort. Purchase revenue and ad revenue from customers who become paying customers within that lifetime are included.
Customers are cohorted by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. The “Customer Lifetime” selector defines the final calendar day included in the LTV calculation. For example, 30 days includes revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after each customer's cohort date.
Customers whose first paid purchase is refunded within the selected Customer Lifetime are removed from the paying-customer count.
Realized LTV per Paying Customer can be used as a tool to understand the profitability of (paid) acquisition, compare the impact of product price changes over time, and much more.

measures.description: Customers whose first paid purchase occurred on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus customers whose first paid purchase was refunded during the same window.
The total gross revenue generated on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, minus refunds processed during the same window.
The average gross revenue per paying customer on calendar days 0 through 30 after the customer cohort date, after subtracting refunds processed during the same window.

mrr.description:
Monthly Recurring Revenue, or MRR, is a way of normalizing the scale of your business to better understand your velocity or size. It doesn't map directly to revenue, but it is a useful standardization.

MRR is computed by "normalizing" subscriptions to a 1-month period. For example, a subscription that is $8 per month, will contribute $8 to MRR while it is active. An annual subscription that costs $120 per year will contribute $10 dollars per month to MRR for 12 months. This normalizing of all durations to a 1 month period makes it easier to compare different subscriptions of different durations together.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, MRR uses the cycle each subscription was in on that date. For example, when a subscription renews from Cycle 1 into Cycle 2, its MRR moves to Cycle 2 on the renewal date; its earlier MRR remains in Cycle 1.

MRR is an important measure because it not only captures the size of your subscriber base, but translates that into a real velocity metric for your business. MRR and ARR are considered the standard velocity metrics for subscription software companies.

measures.description: Monthly Recurring Revenue at the end of the period.

mrr_movement.description:
MRR Movement shows how new subscriptions, resubscriptions, expansion, churn, and contraction affect MRR.

Movement is New MRR + Resubscription MRR + Expansion MRR - Churned MRR - Contraction MRR.

Looking at MRR Movement is important to understand the factors that cause your MRR to increase or decrease over a period and give insight into what grows or contracts your business.

measures.description: MRR contributed by New Subscriptions.
MRR contributed by customers who resubscribed after lapsing.

MRR added when continuing subscriptions begin generating more MRR, such as after product changes, price changes, offer periods, higher-contribution renewals and recoveries, or an exchange rate change causes a subscription to generate more MRR.
MRR removed when paid access ends, a payment is refunded or adjusted downward, or a renewal or billing recovery brings in no revenue.

MRR removed when continuing subscriptions begin generating less MRR, such as after product changes, price changes, offer periods, lower-contribution renewals and recoveries, or an exchange rate change causes a subscription to generate less MRR.
New MRR + Resubscription MRR + Expansion MRR - Churned MRR - Contraction MRR, the net change in MRR during the period.

prediction_explorer.description:
The Prediction Explorer allows you to measure the gross predicted lifetime value (LTV) of various customer cohorts over time to estimate the long-term revenue that may be driven by those cohorts. We generate predicted revenue based on the prior retention rates of subscriptions on the same product, or of a mix of fallback dimensions when sufficient data for the purchased product is unavailable, and then tailoring that prediction based on the cancellation behavior of each individual subscription.

Cohorts can be defined as cohorts of New Customers, Initial Conversions, or New Paying Customers from a given period. Predictions are provided with either a yellow cell shading, indicating a low-volume cohort size where therefore the prediction is low confidence, or a light green cell shading which represent our predictions for cohorts with a sufficient sample size.

Please use caution when making decisions based on predicted future performance, and review the linked documentation below to understand the current limitations of the prediction model.

refund_rate.description:
The Refund Rate chart shows the number of paid subscription transactions and one-time purchases in each time period and what proportion of these transactions was refunded. This includes new subscriptions, renewals, resubscriptions, and paid product changes. Trial starts are excluded because they have no revenue and cannot be refunded.

Refunds are counted in the period of the original paid transaction, not the period when the refund was processed. This means the Refund Rate for a prior period can change when a new refund is recorded. When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, the chart uses the cycle at the time of the original transaction.

The Refund Rate is an important indicator whether your customers are getting the value they expected when they started their subscription.

measures.description: The total number of paid, non-trial subscription transactions and one-time purchases during the period.
The number of transactions that were refunded grouped by the purchase date.
The percentage of transactions from the period that have been refunded. The rate can change later when new refunds are recorded.

refund_request.description:
This chart tracks App Store and Google Play refund and chargeback events. It breaks events down by resolution status—whether the refund was granted, declined, reversed, or is still awaiting the store's decision. Each request is counted in the period RevenueCat received it, and its outcome updates as store notifications arrive.
To receive these events in RevenueCat, configure App Store Server Notifications and Google Play notifications. For the most accurate and timely App Store data, we recommend using Apple's V2 notifications.

measures.description: The number of refund requests granted in the period.

The number of refund requests classified as declined, including store-declined requests and unresolved requests without an observed grant after 2 days for App Store or 7 days for Google Play. Google Play declines are inferred because Google does not send decline events.
The number of refunds reversed in the period.
The number of refund requests without a final outcome that remain within the store's fallback window: 2 days for App Store or 7 days for Google Play.
Total refund requests in the period.

refunds.description: The Refunds chart shows refunds processed during a period, plus downward subscription payment adjustments recorded during that period. Refunded Transactions counts store refund events only. You can select between Refunded Revenue, Refunded Revenue (net of taxes), or Refunded Proceeds as the definition to visualize in the chart.

measures.description: Gross revenue from refunds processed and downward subscription payment adjustments recorded in the period, rounded to the nearest whole number.
The number of store refund events grouped by the date the refund was processed. Downward payment adjustments without a refund event do not increase this count.

revenue.description: Revenue displays the revenue generated during a period. This number will usually be a little higher than MRR as it is un-normalized and all the revenue from an annual subscription is charted the period it starts or is renewed. This chart also displays all revenue from non-consumable and consumable purchases, non-renewing subscriptions, and ads. You can select between Revenue, Revenue (net of taxes), Proceeds, or Gross revenue before refunds as the revenue definition to visualize in the chart. When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, each transaction uses the cycle that applied when it occurred, so later renewals do not move earlier revenue to another cycle.

measures.description: The net revenue generated in a given period; which is total revenue after refunds and downward subscription payment adjustments, minus our estimate of revenue deducted from the stores for taxes and commission.
The count of revenue-generating purchase transactions in the period. Refunds do not reduce this count.
The total number of times ads were successfully displayed to users. Each impression represents one instance of an ad being shown.

subscription_retention.description:
Subscription Retention measures how paying subscriptions renew and retain over time by cohorts.

When segmenting by subscription start date, cohorts are segmented by the start of a paid subscription. Period 0 is the initial paid period; later completed periods show how many subscriptions reached that paid renewal period, whether or not auto-renew is still enabled. When segmenting by other fields, cohorts include all paid subscriptions started within the specified date range and show the portion that reached each paid period out of those with an opportunity to do so.

The final, incomplete period is indicated with a hashed background and shows how many subscriptions are set to renew by the end of the period, taking into account the auto-renewal preference of the subscriptions.

subscription_status.description:
The Subscription Status chart breaks down Active Subscriptions, Active Trials, MRR, ARR, or Subscription Revenue by the current status of the underlying subscription that currently grants access and contributes to that measure.

A subscription will have a status of Billing Issue if it's currently in a grace period or a billing retry where access remains active. Billing retries where access has ended are not included in the chart. Set to Cancel includes subscriptions that will not renew, will pause, or require price-increase consent. Set to Renew includes subscriptions that will renew, change products, or have already renewed. Other states are shown as Unknown.

Each measure can then be filtered or segmented by values like Product Duration, Expiration Month, and more to understand how the portion Set to Cancel or in a Billing Issue state is affected by these dimensions.

When filtering or segmenting by Renewal Cycle, the chart uses the cycle from each subscription's latest current event.

measures.description: The total number of currently active subscriptions.
The number of currently active subscriptions in the Set to Renew status, including subscriptions set to renew, change products, or already renewed.
The number of currently active subscriptions that are set to cancel at the end of their current period.

The number of currently active subscriptions that were set to renew at the end of their prior period, but failed to do so due to a billing issue, and whose access remains active during a grace period or billing retry.
The portion of currently active subscriptions in the Set to Renew status.
measures.display_name: Active Subscriptions Set to Renew Percentage

measures.description: The portion of currently active subscriptions that are set to cancel at the end of their current period.
measures.display_name: Active Subscriptions Set to Cancel Percentage

measures.description: The portion of currently active subscriptions that were set to renew at the end of their prior period, but failed to do so due to a billing issue, and whose access remains active during a grace period or billing retry.

trials.description:
Active Trials shows the number of active trials at the end of the period. This includes all trials, regardless of whether they are set to auto-convert on completion.

The volume of Active Trials is a good leading indicator to growth of Active Subscriptions and therefore MRR. If the volume of active trials is increasing or decreasing it indicates that your business may be accelerating or decelerating respectively. The Active Trials Movement chart can help you understand these movements.

measures.description: The number of free trials granting access at the end of the period.

trials_movement.description:
Active Trials Movement breaks down the inputs to the Active Trials chart and gives you a picture of how your active trial base is evolving.

New Trials includes trial starts and trial-to-trial product changes. Expired Trials includes trials that stopped granting access and product changes away from a trial, reduced by access restorations. Trial-to-trial product changes add one to each side and therefore net to zero in Movement.

Understanding the dynamics of your trial base is important for understanding leading indicators of the growth of your business.

measures.description: Trial starts and trial-to-trial product changes in the period.
Trials that stopped granting access and product changes away from a trial, reduced by access restorations.
New Trials - Expired Trials, the net change in Active Trials during the period.

trials_new.description:
New Trials counts the trials that started during the period. Changing product while staying in a trial is not a new trial and is not counted here; the Active Trials Movement chart includes those, because Active Trials has to move the trial between products.
Unlike the conversion charts, which group customers by the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase, this chart attributes each trial to the date that trial started. Each subscription trial is counted, so a customer who starts trials on two subscriptions contributes two New Trials but only one Trial Start in the Trial Conversion Funnel.
The New Trials chart can be used to track volume in this key top of funnel metric, and segment it by key dimensions for your business to understand what's driving your performance.

measures.description: The number of trials that started in the period.

customers_active.description: Active Customers counts the approximate number of unique customers for whom RevenueCat recorded SDK activity during the selected period. A customer with activity multiple times or on multiple days is counted once in that period. In RevenueCat, the term "customer" refers to the person using an app, regardless of whether they have yet made a purchase. You can use our conversion charts to measure the portion of these customers that then start trials, convert to paid, etc. Data is only accurate for the last 28 days. Data before that may be inaccurate or zero.

measures.description: The approximate number of unique customers for whom RevenueCat recorded SDK activity during the period. Each customer is counted once per period.

trial_conversion.description:
The Trial Conversion Funnel measures the conversion of customers starting free trials, through their conversion into paying subscriptions.

Customers are grouped by their customer cohort date, the earliest date they were first seen or made their first purchase. Each period measures the number of New Customers whose cohort date falls in that period.

A customer enters the funnel when they start a free trial no later than their first conversion. For example, a trial started after the customer already bought a one-time product is excluded. Each qualifying customer contributes once to Started Trials. Their outcome can reflect a later trial. If they abandon the first trial but a later trial becomes their first paid purchase, they are counted as converted, not abandoned.

The Start Rate is a valuable way of measuring how compelling your value proposition is, but Conversion Rate is the real measure of how effectively that value proposition has been delivered through your product during the trial period.

measures.description: The number of new customers whose customer cohort date falls within the period.
The number of customers in the cohort who started at least one qualifying trial.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial converted into a paid subscription. Later refunds do not remove the conversion.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial is active and set to auto-convert on completion.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial is active and not set to auto-convert on completion.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial no longer grants access but is not yet terminal, such as during billing retry or a pause.
The number of those customers whose qualifying trial expired without converting.
The percentage of New Customers who started at least one qualifying trial.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial converted into a paid subscription. Active trials are not yet conversions.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial is active and set to auto-convert.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial is active and not set to auto-convert.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial no longer grants access but is not yet terminal.
The percentage of customers who started a qualifying trial whose trial expired without converting.

trial_conversion_rate.description:
The Trial Conversion Rate chart measures the number of trials that started in a given period, and the portion of them that converted to a paid subscription. Each trial is counted separately.

Trial Conversion Rate is important to track so that you can understand how likelihood to pay changes over time and by various dimensions.

Conversion Rate counts pending trials as not converted, so periods whose trials are still running read low until those trials end. Select Conversion Rate (Completed Trials) to leave pending trials out, which makes recent periods and newly launched stores comparable sooner.

Please note that the number of Trial Starts reported in each period in this chart will differ from the same period of the Trial Conversion Funnel, since the funnel is grouped by customer cohort date—the earliest date a customer was first seen or made their first purchase—not by trial start date.

measures.description: The number of trials that started in the period.
The number of those trials that converted to paid. Later refunds do not remove the conversion.
The number of those trials that expired without converting.
The number of those trials that have not yet converted or expired.
The number of those trials that have converted or expired.
The portion of trials that started in the period that converted to paid. Pending trials count as not converted.

trial_cancellation.description:
The Trial Cancellation chart measures the portion of trials that started in a given period and were canceled within a specified period of time since their start date. Each trial is counted separately.

A "canceled" trial is one that expired without converting to paid, where the customer turned off auto-renewal at some point during the trial (while it still granted access). Cancellations are timed by the customer's last in-trial opt-out, so a trial that is cancelled, re-enabled, and cancelled again is measured by that final cancellation. A trial whose customer opts out but which then converts is not counted as a cancellation.

Cancellation is one of the reasons a trial can expire without converting. The others are shown in the breakdown — billing failures (the payment was in a retry or grace period at expiry) and lapsed trials (expired with no opt-out and no billing signal).

The Cancellation Timeframe selector measures whether the last in-trial opt-out occurred within 1, 2, 5, or 7 days of each trial's start, with each day measured as 24 hours. Unbounded includes an opt-out at any point during the trial.

measures.description: The number of trials that started in the period.
The number of those trials that expired without converting and whose last in-trial opt-out happened within 168 hours of its start.
The number of those trials that expired without converting while payment was in a billing-retry or grace period.
The number of those trials that ended without converting and without an observed opt-out or billing-failure signal, including trials past their end date without a terminal expired event.
The percentage of trials that started in the period that expired without converting and whose last in-trial opt-out happened within 168 hours of its start.

non-subscription_purchases.description: Non-subscription purchases include consumable, non-consumable, lifetime, and non-renewing subscription purchases; none renew automatically.

measures.description: The number of non-subscription purchases that occurred in a period.

ad_revenue.description: Track the total revenue generated from ads in your app. This is your primary monetization metric, showing how much income your ad placements are generating.

measures.description: The total number of times users clicked on ads.
The total number of times ads were displayed to users.
The total amount earned from ads during the period.

ad_impressions.description: Track the total number of times ads were displayed to users in your app. Impressions represent your ad exposure and are the foundation for calculating other key metrics like CTR and eCPM.

measures.description: The total number of times ads were successfully displayed to users. Each impression represents one instance of an ad being shown.

ad_clicks.description: Track the number of times users clicked on ads in your app. Clicks indicate user engagement with ads and can help you understand which ad placements and formats are most effective.

measures.description: The total number of times users clicked on ads. Each click represents a user interaction with an advertisement.

ad_monetized_customers.description: Track the number of unique customers with at least one recorded ad impression. This helps you understand the size of your ad-monetized user base and identify trends in ad engagement.

measures.description: The count of unique customers with at least one recorded ad impression. Each customer is counted once per period, regardless of how many ads they viewed or how much revenue they generated.

paywall_abandonment.description:
Paywall Abandonment measures the proportion of customer-paywall pairs that did not result in an initial conversion on calendar days 0 through 3. It breaks abandonment into purchase cancellations and bounces.

This chart is cohorted by the first paywall impression date for each customer-paywall pair. A pair is abandoned if no initial conversion occurs on calendar days 0 through 3. Total abandonment combines bounced and cancelled pairs.

This chart only tracks impressions and conversions from RevenueCat Paywalls. Paywalls implemented with custom code are not tracked.

Tracking paywall abandonment helps identify friction points in your monetization flow. High bounce rates may indicate pricing or value proposition issues, while high cancellation rates might suggest payment flow problems or buyer's remorse at the final step.

measures.description: The number of unique customer-paywall pairs first seen during the cohort period.
The total number of customer-paywall pairs that bounced or cancelled.
The percentage of customer-paywall pairs that bounced or cancelled.

app_store_save_outcomes.description: App Store Save Outcomes is used with Apple's Retention Message API feature. This chart measures the total number of saved retention messages in each period, broken down by outcome: redeemed promotional offer, redeemed alternate plan, or no purchase.

measures.description: The number of saved retention messages in the period.
